subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time to review Redwood with us today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed SLO checklist to help validate fit with your performance needs. Attaching a one-pager and our performance matrix.

Key items we covered:
- Demo highlights: streaming responses + function/tool calling, prefix KV cache for session reuse, autoscaling options for spike handling.
- Typical Redwood tradeoffs: batching improves cost but increases tail latency; streaming lowers perceived latency for end-users.

Requested info to finalize sizing and MAP:
1) Latency targets (p50/p95/p99) for user-facing flows (streaming vs non-streaming).
2) Expected sustained throughput (requests/min) and peak concurrency.
3) Average and max prompt lengths + expected output token counts.
4) Any hard constraints on cold-start or warm-start latencies (e.g., <200ms p95).
5) Whether streaming is mandatory for the primary flow or optional.

Proposed next steps (short):
- You provide the targets above by EOD Friday.
- We run a short perf run using your profile (we'll need a sample prompt set).
- Share a MAP (mutual action plan) with sizing, timeline, and decision criteria.

Attachments: post-demo-slo-checklist.pdf, redwood-performance-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — I looped in Jonas (solutions lead) and Dev (inference engineer) for any technical follow-ups.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Marissa — great session yesterday. Quick answers below so you can start sizing. Happy to jump on a quick call if anything is unclear.

1) Latency targets (primary user flow - account lookup + contextual response):
- p50: < 60ms (ideal)
- p95: < 180ms (hard requirement)
- p99: < 400ms (we can tolerate some tail but prefer lower)
Streaming: would prefer streaming for faster perceived latency on longer responses; initial token should appear in <150ms.

2) Throughput / concurrency:
- Sustained: ~1,200 requests/min (20 rps)
- Peak bursts: up to 5,000 requests/min (~83 rps) for short windows (2-5 minutes)
- Concurrent sessions expected: ~300 active concurrent calls during peaks

3) Prompt/output sizes:
- Avg prompt: 200 tokens
- Avg response: 150 tokens
- Max response length: 800 tokens (rare)

4) Cold-start constraints: Warm-start p95 should be < 250ms; cold-start acceptable up to 1.5s during scale events.

5) Streaming: strongly preferred for the primary flow (chat-like UX).

Related items: sample prompt set attached (I’ll upload to the Drive link). We also need to understand how Redwood handles prefix KV caching across user sessions — does cache hit rate persist across requests for the same user?

—Alex
Product Lead, FintechCo
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Alex — thanks for the detailed targets, that’s super helpful. Quick technical notes and assumptions before we run a perf validation: 

- Streaming: we can deliver first byte sub-150ms in many cases, but that depends on model choice and prompt length. For long responses (>>300 tokens) streaming amortizes perceived latency — good match to your UX ask.
- Throughput: we recommend a dedicated pool with autoscaling for your peak bursts. For sustained 20 rps and peaks ~83 rps, our sizing estimate (rough) is 2-3 A100-equivalent slots with burst capacity. We’ll firm this up after a targeted load run.
- Concurrency: 300 concurrent sessions is within expected scale but we’ll validate memory/KV cache sizing — Dev, can you prepare a perf run config that simulates: 20 rps sustained, 83 rps burst (2 minutes), payload distrib as Alex specified, and streaming enabled?
- Cache: prefix KV caching is session-scoped by default; we can persist warm KV for returning users using sticky routing. Cache hit-rate depends on session stickiness and prompt patterns; we’ll instrument this and share expected hit-rate projections.

Next steps (internal + customer MAP items):
1) Dev to run perf job (simulate streaming + burst pattern) — target run by Tue 25 May.
2) Marissa to share decision criteria doc (we’ll include latency/throughput, cost/cpu tradeoffs, and fallbacks).
3) Alex to upload sample prompt set to the Drive link and confirm whether there are any PII constraints.

I’ll start drafting the MAP once we have the perf results.

—Jonas
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 07:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi all — I kicked off a preliminary perf job in our staging cluster to mirror Alex’s profile. Summary of config and early observations below. Full run artifacts are linked in the Drive folder.

Test config:
- Model: open-llama-70b-quant (quantized) as a proxy for target latency; we'll also test a lower-latency distilled variant.
- Streaming: enabled
- Workload: 20 rps sustained, 83 rps bursts for 2 minutes every 10 minutes over 30 minutes total
- Tokens: prompt 200 avg / response 150 avg; max 800 tokens
- Concurrency simulated: 300 sessions

Early results (best-effort, 1st pass):
- p50: 55ms; p95: 170ms; p99: 380ms (streaming enabled) — these are within Alex’s stated requirements for warm starts.
- First-byte latency: median 120ms, 95th 220ms (depends on model variant).
- Memory: KV cache per-session sizing looks acceptable; with stickiness we saw ~60% hit-rate on a simulated returning cohort (we'll refine).

Artifacts: perf logs and consolidated CSV are in Drive: https://drive.google.com/fintechco-perf-artifacts. I’ll produce a short summary PDF and a sizing recommendation (expected slots, expected monthly compute estimate) by EOD.

Couple questions for Alex: any dedicated compliance requirements for storing sample prompts (if they have PII we can keep them in customer-managed bucket), and do you want us to include a canary plan for cutover?

—Dev
Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: perf-run-logs.zip (link in Drive)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround and for uploading the prompt set. Based on Dev’s prelim run and Jonas’s notes, I’ll draft the MAP and decision criteria doc this morning. Proposed decision criteria (short):
- Performance fit: p95 warm < 200ms with streaming for primary flow
- Scalability: ability to handle 5k rps bursts with autoscaling and predictable cost estimate
- Cost: total monthly inference cost within your procurement guardrails (I’ll include a cost vs latency matrix)
- Operational controls: sticky routing for cache hit improvements, logging/traceability for audits
- Security: confirmation on PII storage approach (customer-managed bucket preferred)

Next steps from me:
1) Share MAP + decision criteria doc by EOD today (link added to HubSpot and Drive).
2) Dev to finalize perf-run summary and sizing recommendation (ETA EOD).
3) Schedule a follow-up to review results and finalize procurement timeline — proposed Wed 26 May, 10am PT.

If those items look good, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks all — looking forward to closing this out.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
